summary: Iteration 6 (driver documents + blocking + admin review + selfie + Waze/Google Maps + in-app route) — Backend PASS 19/19 pytest, Frontend PARTIAL PASS on the flows testable via web preview. Backend suite (/app/backend/tests/test_documents.py, 8 test classes, 19 tests, ~9 s wall clock) validates every spec item end-to-end against the public preview: (1) GET /api/documents/types returns exactly 8 keys (id_card, driving_license, vtc_card, rc_pro, registration, vehicle_insurance, rc_circulation, technical_inspection); (2) Fresh driver via /api/auth/register → GET /api/documents/mine returns blocked=true with blocking list containing 'Pièce d'identité', 'Carte grise', 'Assurance du véhicule', 'RC Circulation' and 'RC Pro (Responsabilité Civile Professionnelle)' (since manager_id is null → independent). POST /api/driver/status {is_online:true} → 423 with 'bloqué' message; GET /api/rides/available → 423; (3) POST /api/documents/upload multipart (PNG, type=driving_license, valid_until=now+20d) → 200 item state 'expiring' and expiring array non-empty; upload without valid_until for an expiring type → 422 'Date d'expiration requise'; upload with content-type text/plain → 415 'Format accepté : JPG, PNG, WEBP ou PDF'; upload type=registration without dates → 200 state 'valid'; (4) POST /api/documents/vtc_card/not-applicable → 200 state 'not_applicable'; POST /api/documents/id_card/not-applicable → 409 'Ce document est obligatoire'; (5) After uploading id_card, driving_license, rc_pro, vehicle_insurance, rc_circulation (all valid+180d) + registration (no expiry) + N/A vtc_card + N/A technical_inspection → blocked=false, POST /api/driver/status is_online=true → 200; (6) Admin (chauffeur@test.com moderator): GET /api/admin/drivers lists the new driver with blocked flag; GET /api/admin/drivers/{id}/documents populates file_path on every doc item; GET /api/files/{path}?token= returns Content-Type image/png; PATCH /api/admin/documents/{doc_id} {status:'rejected', note:'illisible'} → blocked=true and a 'document' notification is emitted; re-uploading the rejected doc → blocked=false; non-moderator PATCH → 403; (7) Selfie: POST /api/admin/drivers/{id}/request-selfie → 200; driver GET /documents/mine has selfie_requested=true and a notification of type 'selfie'; driver POST /documents/upload type=selfie → selfie.status='pending', selfie_requested=false; admin PATCH selfie doc status=valid → selfie.status='valid'; (8) Upload valid_until in the past (mandatory type) → state 'expired' + blocked=true; (9) GET /api/geo/route?from=48.8443,2.3743&to=48.8584,2.2945 returns coords array (>2), distance_km, duration_min (real OSRM response, no fallback). Frontend (web 390×844, EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL): chauffeur@test.com login OK; Documents tab shows documents-screen with compliant-banner (all docs valid) — needed a ~2 s wait after screen mount for /documents/mine to resolve; tap doc-upload-id_card opens SheetModal doc-editor exposing pick-camera + pick-library + doc-valid-until + doc-save; sheet-close dismisses the sheet gracefully (web file picker cannot be automated, as expected). Profile: driver-profile-screen shows nav-preference block with both nav-waze and nav-gmaps buttons (44px pill height OK); open-drivers-admin opens drivers-admin SheetModal listing 31 admin-driver-* rows (matching admin API); tapping the chauffeur@test.com row opens admin-driver-detail with 8 admin-doc-* cards and the request-selfie button. Not automatable on web: full-page reload for nav-preference persistence (React Native web state re-mounts to a different tab-group route on reload → couldn't cleanly re-locate nav-waze bg color post-reload; the underlying AsyncStorage read + branch is a simple `getNavApp() → setNav()` in profile.tsx, no functional risk). Register-a-fresh-driver via UI: the register form uses different testIDs than expected (no `full-name-input`, `vehicle-model-input`, `license-plate-input`) so I couldn't drive the whole fresh-driver-blocked-banner UI flow end-to-end — but the exact same flow is covered by pytest (blocked=true on GET /documents/mine + 423 on POST /driver/status) and the UI branch in `app/(driver)/index.tsx` is a straightforward `activeCompliance.blocked ? <docs-blocked-banner /> : …`. Same for the active-ride navigate-button (create passenger ride → accept → click nav-button → verify window.open URL contains waze.com/google.com/maps) — the code path in files.ts.openNavigation is trivial and the backend /rides & /geo/route pieces are all validated by pytest.

issues: Recurring RN-Web deprecation warning (carry-over from iter-3/4): 'shadow*' style props deprecated, use 'boxShadow'.
Compliance banner only appears after /documents/mine resolves (~1-2 s); the ActivityIndicator is centered but there is no skeleton for the banner area — minor perceived-latency polish.

action_items: LOW: expose testIDs `full-name-input`, `vehicle-model-input`, `license-plate-input` on the register form so the fresh-driver-blocked-banner UI flow can be automated on web preview.
LOW (carry-over): migrate remaining `shadow*` StyleSheet props to `boxShadow`.
critical_code_review_comments: documents.py evaluate_driver correctly persists `docs_blocked` and force-sets `is_online=false` in the same $set when blocking — no race between /driver/status and the compliance sweep.
documents.py is_required(if_independent) uses `not driver.get('manager_id')` — team-managed drivers (equipier@test.com) are exempted from RC Pro; independent drivers are required, verified.

documents.py delete_many before insert_one on upload guarantees only one doc per (driver, type). On re-upload of a rejected doc the old row (with status=rejected + storage_path) is dropped, which cleanly resets warned_30/status — good.

documents.py get_file allows either the doc owner OR any is_moderator to read; token is accepted via query param (thanks to current_user query-token support) — this enables <Image src={fileUrl(path, token)} /> in DriversAdmin without a fetch+base64 dance.

storage.py wraps requests in run_in_threadpool + retries once on 503 after re-init — sensible for the Emergent object-storage proxy; 402 quota-full is correctly surfaced as 'Quota de stockage épuisé' to the client.
geo_routes.geo_route degrades gracefully to a straight-line 2-point coord array with fallback=true when OSRM is unreachable, so the map layer in the driver home never breaks the ride flow.
documents.py compliance_sweep runs unauthenticated per-driver (send_alerts=True) — make sure server.py registers it in the startup loop (already the case in iter-4 with reminder_loop pattern).

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (documents-screen + editor + drivers-admin + admin-driver-detail + nav preference UI all working; register-form testIDs missing prevented driving the fresh-driver blocked-banner UI end-to-end; active-ride navigate-button flow not exercised on web)

seed_data_creation: Created 3 throwaway drivers via /api/auth/register: TEST_drv_<ts>@test.com (blocked scenario), TEST_drv_<ts>_compl@test.com (compliance flow, admin review + selfie), TEST_drv_<ts>_exp@test.com (expired-date scenario). All are pure test rows in the users+documents collections; they do not touch chauffeur@test.com. Verified at the end of the run: chauffeur@test.com is left with blocked=false, blocking=[], selfie_requested=false, expiring=[] (per curl to /documents/mine).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-6 acceptance is met on the backend for every spec item. Frontend gaps left for main agent to self-verify quickly in Expo Go or the web preview: (a) fresh driver registration → driver-home shows docs-blocked-banner + online-toggle routes to Documents; (b) nav-preference persistence after reload; (c) active-ride navigate-button opens waze.com/google.com/maps URL and the '🛣️ Itinéraire' route line appears. Pytest suite is idempotent (uses fresh-registered emails each run) and safe to rerun; single-worker mode is required — `pytest backend/tests/test_documents.py -n 0` — because module-scoped fixtures share state across classes (LoadScope parallel scheduling breaks fixture-shared state assumptions on this file).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs. Two initial pytest failures were purely test-authoring: (i) auth response uses `access_token`, not `token` (fixed to accept either); (ii) admin listing lowercases emails, so the assert must be case-insensitive (fixed). Both fixed inline before finalising the report.
